clue.text: It could spoil what's programmed for tomorrow

definitions.text: It could spoil what's programmed for tomorrow

parts.words: It could spoil what's programmed for tomorrow
parts.note: reads like a threat to tomorrow's TV schedule, but means a computer fault feared to wreck software when the date rolled over to the year 2000

explanation.surface: Something threatens to ruin the TV schedule planned for tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on 31 December 1999, so 'tomorrow' was 1 January 2000, when computers storing years as two digits were expected to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Y2K glitch was a feared software fault that could wreck date-dependent programs at the rollover to 2000.

clue.text: Show good girls an old instrument

parts.note: a musical is a stage show with songs
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A show features good girls playing an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of tuned drinking vessels played by rubbing wet fingers round the rims was a fashionable eighteenth-century instrument.

clue.text: A Christmassy chap upset her

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word for the chap is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: Noel is a boy's name linked with Christmas

explanation.surface: A festive fellow has upset some woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel, French for Christmas, is a name given to boys born then; 'upset' turns it bottom to top in this down clue, and 'her' stands for any woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a woman's name, so a pronoun for a female person stands in for it.

clue.text: Distress and fear one may get tonight, for example

indicators.note: to distress is to batter or damage, so the following words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone warns of misery and fear that may arrive tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' rearranges AND FEAR ONE. The puzzle ran on 31 December 1999, so 'tonight' was the close of the old millennium; 'may get' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The last night of 1999 marked the close of a historical period, the passing of an age.

clue.text: It's very close, not far across the river

indicators.note: the word for not far is stretched across the river, holding it inside

parts.note: near means not far
the Wye is a river on the English-Welsh border

explanation.surface: Something is near at hand, just over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wye is a river in Wales and western England, a favourite crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: On 31 December the turn of the year is imminent, only hours away.

clue.text: Improving performance in cups, win games

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A team on the up wins cup ties and matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'cUPS WIN Games'.
explanation.definitionFit: An upswing is an upward trend, a recovery in fortunes or results.

clue.text: Give instructions to cut cheese

indicators.note: cut here means docked, so the last letter of the word for giving instructions is chopped off

parts.note: to brief someone is to give them instructions

explanation.surface: Someone directs staff how to slice the cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' removes the final F from BRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese from the region of the same name.

clue.text: Like modern arrangement of dates, with a choice of boys

parts.note: Greg is a boy's name
or offers a choice between alternatives
Ian is another boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl's calendar is filled with dates with a selection of boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boys' supplies two names with 'a choice of' (OR) between them; 'dates' looks romantic but means the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gregorian calendar, introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582, is the modern system for ordering dates.

clue.text: Building done with minimum chaos, with lines heading East put in?

indicators.note: put in means these extra letters are inserted into the jumble
chaos means disorder, so the letters of done and minimum are jumbled

parts.note: L is short for line, so LL is lines

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A building is completed with little fuss, with extra lines added by eastern contractors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' scrambles the two plain words; 'put in' slips the lines and the 'heading' of East into the jumble, and 'Building' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant tent-like structure at Greenwich was built to house London's celebration of the year 2000.

clue.text: Way reverse of fortune on board produces decisive situations

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting inside the letters that stand for it

parts.note: to be on board is to be on a ship, and SS is a steamship
how means way or manner
a down is a setback or reverse, as in ups and downs

explanation.surface: A card player suffers a reversal of fortune at the gaming board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention for going inside SS (steamship); HOW and DOWN sit between the two S's.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a final confrontation that settles a dispute.

clue.text: Britons of the first millennium taking rocks to part of Ireland

parts.note: ice is served 'on the rocks', so rocks means ice
NI stands for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Ancient Britons ship rocks over to Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' is bar slang for ice cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a tribe of East Anglia, led by Boudicca against Rome in the first century AD.

clue.text: Hard to get into restaurant commonly? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the letter for hard enters the word for the eatery, sitting inside it

parts.note: caff is a colloquial word for a cafe
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone complains that it is hard to get a table at a cheap restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'caff' is British slang for a cheap cafe; H goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is husks separated from grain, hence worthless stuff, idle banter or rubbish.

clue.text: Man of the millennium?

indicators.note: of here means taken from, the answer being a part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Who will be named the outstanding man of the millennium?
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'thE MILlennium'. 'Man of the millennium' reads as an award, but 'Man' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a male first name, as in Emil and the Detectives.

clue.text: Aim to depart before 3.15

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Aim to depart before 3.15 (4)' for GOAL: GO (depart) is clear, but no reading of '3.15' giving AL was found in the scan or by search.

clue.text: Bottle of wine — he bought it some years before reaching millennium

definitions.meaning: a very large wine bottle holding eight standard bottles

definitions.text: he bought it some years before reaching millennium
definitions.meaning: the biblical patriarch died at 969, some years short of a thousand; 'bought it' is slang for died

explanation.walkthrough: 'bought it' looks like a purchase of the wine, but means 'died'.
explanation.definitionFit: Big wine bottles are named after biblical figures, and the patriarch who lived longest of all is one.

clue.text: Beginner who's paid a pound?

parts.note: L stands for a pound, from Latin libra
an earner is someone who is paid

explanation.surface: A novice asks whether they are earning a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a pound sterling comes from the Latin libra; L also marks a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice still acquiring a skill is a learner.

clue.text: Setting about very long fish

parts.note: assai is the musical term for very, as in allegro assai
the ling is a long slender fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone is laying into a lengthy fish.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSAI is an Italian musical direction meaning 'very'; 'long' describes the fish rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To set about someone is to attack them, which is what assailing means.

clue.text: Classic that makes English racing special

indicators.note: special suggests something specially made over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A classic race makes English racing distinctive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges E (English) with RACING. 'Classic' looks like a horse race but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical means belonging to ancient Greece or Rome, and Grecian refers to the Greek side of that.

clue.text: Distinctions — several hundreds of them in 2000

definitions.meaning: honour or glory, the shine of renown
periods of five years; two thousand years hold four hundred of them

explanation.walkthrough: A lustre (lustrum) is a five-year period, so 2000 years contain 400.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory and renown are figurative shine; the second sense is an old word for a half-decade.

clue.text: Instruction not to correct boy under head's protection

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for boy is placed below the instruction

parts.note: stet, Latin for 'let it stand', tells a printer to ignore a correction
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A headteacher tells staff not to correct a boy under their protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head's protection' looks like a headteacher's care but means a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat covers and shields the head.

clue.text: People as found, note, round centre of Ghana

indicators.note: round means the first pieces surround the middle of the country name

parts.note: taken as written
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the centre of a word is all of it but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A people are found in the heart of Ghana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is padding; 'round' wraps AS and the sol-fa note around the heart of Ghana's name, and 'People' is a nation, not persons in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashanti are a nation of central Ghana, once a powerful West African kingdom.

clue.text: A resting-place I provided for South American rodent

parts.note: a couch is a place to rest

explanation.surface: Somebody offers a bed and lodging for a small animal from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The acouchi is a small agouti-like rodent of tropical South American forests.

clue.text: Female undergarment you might spot in millennium

definitions.meaning: a woman's light underskirt or petticoat
an error, since the word is often misspelt with one N

explanation.walkthrough: 'millennium' is often written with a single N, a mistake you might spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a petticoat and a small error.

clue.text: In 2000, English band of little note

indicators.note: in means the letter for English goes inside the Roman numeral for two thousand

parts.note: MM is 2000 in Roman numerals
O is a ring shape, so a band

explanation.surface: In the year 2000 an English group will barely be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside MM, then O, a ring, is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a brief written message or memorandum.

clue.text: Group of colonists fighting in second millennium, originally

indicators.note: in means the word for fighting goes between the other letters
originally points to the opening letter of the word

parts.note: war is fighting

explanation.surface: Colonists fight on into the second millennium.
explanation.walkthrough: WAR goes between S and M (the first letter of millennium). 'colonists' sounds human but means bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a mass of bees leaving to found a new colony.

clue.text: One's covered by Jack and Bill — you can count on them

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letter for one sits beneath the others, covered by them

parts.note: AB (able seaman) is a sailor, as is a jack
AC is short for account, a bill
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is sheltered by two friends, Jack and Bill, who are dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Bill look like two men, but give AB and AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Abacuses are bead frames used for counting.

clue.text: Composer from start of Christian era

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: an age is an era

explanation.surface: A composer from the dawn of the Christian era.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer, known for 4'33".

clue.text: 'e meets Lambeth girl, or one from Lissom Grove

parts.note: the dropped H of Cockney speech leaves just E
Liza of Lambeth is Somerset Maugham's first novel

explanation.surface: A Cockney chap meets a girl from Lambeth, or else one from a London backstreet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth and Lisson Grove are London districts; Shaw's Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion comes from Lisson Grove, printed here as 'Lissom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's flower girl in Pygmalion lived in Lisson Grove, London.

clue.text: Dance in social I organised

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arranged a dance at a social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges IN SOCIAL I.
explanation.definitionFit: The siciliano is a slow pastoral dance from Sicily in compound time.

clue.text: What will mark the start of the new millennium? Exactly!

definitions.text: What will mark the start of the new millennium? Exactly!

parts.words: What will mark the start of the new millennium? Exactly!
parts.note: the stroke of midnight is timed precisely by the clock standard set at the observatory on the Thames prime meridian

explanation.surface: Everyone waits for the precise moment the millennium begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The meridian at Greenwich in London sets the world's time standard, which fixes the exact instant of midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: The time standard measured at the Royal Observatory defines precisely when the new year begins.
